title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with funding rounds and strategic partnerships, while budget allocations hint at a growing focus on resilience and readiness. Meanwhile, international cooperation and competition continue to shape the landscape.

themes.title: Funding Rounds Galore
themes.body: Katalyst Space's recent $12 million raise for a GEO servicing demo mission and True Anomaly's $190 million Series C indicate investors are still keen on space ventures. The Defense-Tech IPO window cracking open adds to the optimism, albeit cautiously.

themes.title: Strategic Partnerships Emerge
themes.body: Anduril and L3Harris teaming up for a tactical SDA constellation bid signals a shift towards collaborative defense initiatives. Similarly, PiLogic's partnership with an Air Force lab for satellite fault-prediction software underscores the military's interest in tech innovation.

themes.title: Budget Boosts for Space Resilience
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup, which adds $1.4 billion to the space resilience line, reflects a growing recognition of the strategic importance of space. This funding could bolster national security efforts amid increasing global competition.

themes.title: International Tensions in Orbit
themes.body: Recent reports of Russian co-orbital activity near commercial GEO slots raise eyebrows and highlight the geopolitical stakes in space. Meanwhile, GPS jamming over the Eastern Med returning to pre-2024 levels serves as a reminder of ongoing operational challenges.
